arxiv-2201-08251.title: Why should we search for vector-like leptons?
arxiv-2201-08251.creator: Feyza Baspehlivan, Burak Dagli, Osman Emre Delialioglu, Saleh Sultansoy
arxiv-2201-08251.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Feyza Baspehlivan, Burak Dagli, Osman Emre Delialioglu, Saleh Sultansoy. There are two strong arguments in favor of vector-like leptons and quarks: Flavor Democracy call for them, and E 6 E_{6} GUT predicts existence of iso-singlet quarks and iso-doublet leptons.

arxiv-2209-03247.title: Some extensions of Krasnoselskii’s fixed point result for real functions
arxiv-2209-03247.creator: Hassan Khandani
arxiv-2209-03247.description: Abstract We extend Krasnoselskii’s fixed point result to non-self-real functions. We find a new and simple proof for Hillam’s result. In our approach, we don’t assume the image of the related mapping to be compact or bounded. In this way, we extend Hillam’s result to self-mappings on ℝ \mathbb{R} .

arxiv-2212-08776.title: A new hybrid mass-flux/ high-order turbulence closure for ocean vertical mixing
arxiv-2212-08776.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by . While various parameterizations of vertical turbulent fluxes at different levels of complexity have been proposed, each has its own limitations. For example, simple first-order closure schemes such as the K-Profile Parameterization (KPP) lack energetic constraints; two-equation models like k − ε k-\varepsilon directly solve an equation for the turbulent kinetic energy but do not account for non-local fluxes, and high-order closures that include the non-local transport terms are computationally expensive.

arxiv-2308-03892.title: Scalable and Equitable Math Problem Solving Strategy Prediction in Big Educational Data
arxiv-2308-03892.creator: Anup Shakya Vasile Rus Deepak Venugopal
arxiv-2308-03892.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Anup Shakya Vasile Rus Deepak Venugopal. Understanding a student’s problem-solving strategy can have a significant impact on effective math learning using Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITSs) and Adaptive Instructional Systems (AISs). For instance, the ITS/AIS can better personalize itself to correct specific misconceptions that are indicated by incorrect strategies, specific problems can be designed to improve strategies and frustration can be minimized by adapting to a student’s natural way of thinking rather than trying to fit a standard strategy for all.

arxiv-2404-03118.title: LVLM-Interpret: An Interpretability Tool for Large Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2404-03118.creator: Gabriela Ben Melech Stan Estelle Aflalo Raanan Yehezkel Rohekar Anahita Bhiwandiwalla, Shao-Yen Tseng Matthew Lyle Olson Yaniv Gurwicz Chenfei Wu Nan Duan Vasudev Lal
arxiv-2404-03118.description: Abstract In the rapidly evolving landscape of artificial intelligence, multi-modal large language models are emerging as a significant area of interest. These models, which combine various forms of data input, are becoming increasingly popular. However, understanding their internal mechanisms remains a complex task.

pmc-10570274.title: InSAR-observed surface deformation in New Mexico’s Permian Basin shows threats and opportunities presented by leaky injection wells
pmc-10570274.creator: E. J. Graves, A. Rinehart, R. Grapenthin, M. F. Angarita, J. Grigg
pmc-10570274.description: Knowledge of aquifer dynamics, including groundwater storage changes, is key to effective groundwater resource and reservoir management. Resolving and accurate modeling of these processes requires knowledge of subsurface poroelastic properties and lateral heterogeneity within units of interest. Computationally demanding methods for determining lateral heterogeneity in poroelastic properties exist but remain difficult to practically employ.

pmc-10601222.title: Xpert MTB/RIF assay for the differential diagnosis between sarcoidosis and tuberculosis intrathoracic lymphadenopathy
pmc-10601222.creator: Xian He, Yuan Zhang, Ying Zhou, Li Li, Qiuhong Li
pmc-10601222.description: BackgroundThe aim of this study was to evaluate the role of Xpert MTB/RIF assay in the detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis for differentiating tuberculosis intrathoracic lymphadenopathy from sarcoidosis intrathoracic lymphadenopathy.MethodsThe patients who were suspected to having sarcoidosis or tuberculosis intrathoracic lymphadenopathy at the Shanghai Pulmonary Hospital between October 1, 2020 and June 30, 2021 were retrospectively evaluated in this study.

pmc-10617096.title: In-organoid single-cell CRISPR screening reveals determinants of hepatocyte differentiation and maturation
pmc-10617096.creator: Junbo Liang, Jinsong Wei, Jun Cao, Jun Qian, Ran Gao, Xiaoyu Li, Dingding Wang, Yani Gu, Lei Dong, Jia Yu, Bing Zhao, Xiaoyue Wang
pmc-10617096.description: BackgroundHarnessing hepatocytes for basic research and regenerative medicine demands a complete understanding of the genetic determinants underlying hepatocyte differentiation and maturation. Single-cell CRISPR screens in organoids could link genetic perturbations with parallel transcriptomic readout in single cells, providing a powerful method to delineate roles of cell fate regulators.

pmc-10744806.title: Research on the Adhesion Properties of Fast-Melting SBS-Modified Asphalt–Aggregate Based on Surface Free Energy Theory
pmc-10744806.creator: Bo Men, Fei Guo, Xiaolong Kang, Jinchao Yue
pmc-10744806.description: In order to study the adhesion properties of fast-melting SBS-modified asphalt (SBS-T) at the interface with aggregates, the contact angles of three dosages of SBS-T asphalt with three liquids (distilled water, glycerol, and formamide) were determined by the sessile drop method based on surface free energy theory.

pmc-11330035.title: Regional differences in frailty among older adults with type 2 diabetes: a multicenter cross-sectional study in Japan
pmc-11330035.creator: Akiko Nishimura, Chie Masuda, Chiyo Murauchi, Miho Ishii, Yuko Murata, Terumi Kawasaki, Mayumi Azuma, Hidenori Arai, Shin-ichi Harashima
pmc-11330035.description: BackgroundSocial environment may broadly impact multifaceted frailty; however, how environmental differences influence frailty in older adults with diabetes remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate regional differences in frailty in urban and rural areas among older adults with diabetes.MethodsThis cross-sectional study was conducted as part of the frailty prevention program for older adults with diabetes study.

pmc-11440604.title: Kinetic Study of OH Radical Reactions with Cyclopentenone Derivatives
pmc-11440604.creator: Patrick Rutto, Emmanuel Ubana, Talitha M Selby, Fabien Goulay
pmc-11440604.description: We investigated the reactions of the hydroxyl radical (OH) with cyclopentenone derivatives and cyclopentanone in a quasi–static reaction cell at 4 Torr across a 300–500 K temperature range. The OH radicals were generated using pulsed laser photolysis of hydrogen peroxide vapors, and the ketone reactants were introduced in excess.

pmc-11479613.title: Investigating the association between osteopenia and bowel perforation through a multicenter radiologic analysis
pmc-11479613.creator: Sebastian Sanduleanu, Koray Ersahin, Jonathan Kottlors, Johannes Bremm, Narmin Talibova, Tim Damer, Merve Erdogan, Nils Groβe Hokamp, Lukas Goertz, Nijat Nasirov, Vilayat Valiyev, Christiane Bruns, David Maintz, Nuran Abdullayev
pmc-11479613.description: Anecdotal evidence from preliminary observations has noted multiple instances where osteoporosis is present in elderly patients before the clinical detection of bowel disease, even in the absence of overt gastrointestinal symptoms. However, any potential association between these conditions remains to be further investigated.

pmc-11527921.title: Neonatal and early infancy antibiotic exposure is associated with childhood atopic dermatitis, wheeze and asthma
pmc-11527921.creator: Santeri Räty, Helena Ollila, Olli Turta, Anna Pärtty, Ville Peltola, Hanna Lagström, Johanna Lempainen, Samuli Rautava
pmc-11527921.description: Antibiotics are frequently administered in the neonatal period and early infancy. Little is known about the long-term health consequences of early life antibiotic exposure. The objective is to investigate the association between neonatal and early life (0–6 months) antibiotic treatment and the development of atopic dermatitis, asthma and the use of inhaled corticosteroid medication later in childhood.

pmc-11610067.title: Achieving adherence to positive airway pressure in commercial drivers using an employer-mandated remote management programme
pmc-11610067.creator: Elizabeth Kneeland, Nadia Ali, David G. Maislin, Yoon Hee Chang, Joyce Epelboim, Brendan T. Keenan, Allan I. Pack
pmc-11610067.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundObstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) is common in commercial drivers, and associated with increased risk of crashes if untreated, making diagnosis and effective treatment crucial in this population.Study design and methodsThis is a retrospective summary of a clinical programme based on telemedicine and remote treatment monitoring developed with a national trucking company to screen new hires in the USA for OSA and implement positive airway pressure (PAP) management. New hires were informed of the programme and consented as part of their employment.

pmc-12389050.title: Use of Factorial Designs to Reduce Stability Studies for Parenteral Drug Products: Determination of Factor Effects via Accelerated Stability Data Analysis
pmc-12389050.creator: Lara Pavčnik, Simona Bohanec, Tina Trdan Lušin, Robert Roškar, René Holm
pmc-12389050.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Objectives: This study explores the potential of factorial analysis as an alternative strategy for optimizing stability study designs for registration batches—an approach not currently addressed in ICH Q1D, which focuses solely on bracketing and matrixing. The objective is to assess the reliability of stability designs reduced based on factorial analysis and the extent to which long-term stability testing can be reduced using this approach.

pmc-12564927.title: Beyond Antioxidants: The Emerging Role of Nrf2 Activation in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)
pmc-12564927.creator: Minoo Sharbafshaaer, Roberta Pepe, Rosaria Notariale, Fabrizio Canale, Gioacchino Tedeschi, Alessandro Tessitore, Paolo Bergamo, Francesca Trojsi, Stergios Boussios
pmc-12564927.description: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a neurodegenerative disorder involving the progressive degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons. While oxidative stress, RNA-binding protein (RBP) pathology, mitochondrial dysfunction, and glial–neuronal dysregulation is involved in ALS pathogenesis, current therapies provide limited benefit, underscoring the need for multi-target disease-modifying strategies.

pmc-12581579.title: Application of diffusion kurtosis imaging in differentiating T0-T1 from T2 rectal tumors
pmc-12581579.creator: Yu-ru Ma, Zhi-wen Zhang, Zi-qiang Wen, Xin-ni Cai, Xue-han Wu, Yu-tao Que, Wen-jie Fan, Quan-meng Liu, Yi-yan Liu, Shen-ping Yu, Yan Chen
pmc-12581579.description: BackgroundHigh-spatial-resolution T2-weighted imaging (HR-T2WI) has been demonstrated to overestimate the staging of early rectal cancer, which could lead to missed opportunities for organ-preserving treatments. This study aimed to investigate the value of diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI) in distinguishing between T0-T1 and T2 rectal tumors.

pmc-12589148.title: Seeing Beyond the Tract: The Superiority of 3 Tesla (3T) MRI Over X-ray Fistulography in Perianal Fistula Evaluation
pmc-12589148.creator: Sachin Khanduri, Mohammad Shahbaz, Sana, Archiya Habib, Somya Singhal, Akshay Aggarwal, Nisha, Avani Kanojia, Kunal N Dwari, Saleem Khan
pmc-12589148.description: BackgroundPerianal fistulas are a prevalent anorectal condition, often resulting from cryptoglandular infections. They cause significant morbidity due to chronic discharge, pain, and recurrent infections, affecting patient's quality of life. Accurate preoperative imaging is crucial for defining the fistulous tract, identifying internal and external openings, and planning surgical intervention to prevent recurrence.

pmc-13285618.title: Efficacy of Valsartan-HCTZ in hypertension: a cohort study exploring age as a key determinant
pmc-13285618.creator: Abdur Rauf, Yasar Shah, Zaki Ullah, Fawad Inayat, Wahby M Babaresh, Aiman Begum, Salman Ahmad
pmc-13285618.description: BackgroundHypertension is a major global public health challenge, and effective management of antihypertensive treatment response is crucial. This study aimed to analyze the demographic, clinical, and lifestyle factors influencing treatment response in hypertensive patients receiving Valsartan monotherapy or Valsartan/Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) combination therapy.

pmc-13295758.title: Spatiotemporal Patterns of Suitable Wintering Habitats for the White-Naped Cranes Under Climate and Land-Use Change
pmc-13295758.creator: He Xiao, Mingqin Shao, Zeng Jiang

pmc-13454337.title: Bridging antiviral drug discovery with a large language model-powered framework
pmc-13454337.creator: Boming Kang, Yang Zhao, Xingyu Chen, Rui Fan, Chunmei Cui, Fuping You, Qinghua Cui
pmc-13454337.description: Viral infections pose ongoing threats to human health, emphasizing the continued need for effective antivirals. Antiviral drug discovery often relies on phenotype-based drug discovery (PBDD) and target-based drug discovery (TBDD). However, current computational approaches focus solely on predicting compounds that bind to specific antiviral-related targets, overlooking the biological relevance of antiviral phenotypes.
